**A language model can improve grammar while making a transcript less faithful.** If the audio says an unusual name, a post-corrector may replace it with a familiar one. If the recognizer is uncertain about a number, the corrector may choose a plausible value with unjustified confidence. The goal is recovering spoken content, not writing the most natural sentence. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.04356)

Suppose the original transcript says “ship fifteen units” with low confidence on the number. A context-only corrector sees that previous orders were fifty and changes it to “fifty.” The result reads well but may be wrong. Without audio or a supported alternative hypothesis, the correction has no decisive evidence.

Constrain edits using N-best candidates, phonetic similarity, timestamps, and confidence. Preserve high-confidence spans and require stronger evidence for names, numbers, and negation. Keep the original transcript and mark unresolved uncertainty rather than filling gaps with fluent guesses.

**Measure harmful edits explicitly.** Count initially correct spans made incorrect, not only initially incorrect spans repaired. Evaluate silence and noisy audio, where hallucinated content is especially revealing. Compare against human audio-grounded references rather than relying solely on a text judge that may favor fluency. Added model calls also affect latency and data handling. A lower language-model loss is not proof of a better transcript.

**Technical details and references.**

A post-corrector can turn an uncertain transcript into a confidently wrong sentence, change numbers/negation, or insert contextually plausible words absent from the audio. Added model calls also increase latency and privacy exposure. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.04356)

Constrain candidates using N-best hypotheses, aligned timestamps, phonetic similarity, and a small edit budget. Preserve high-confidence spans and expose unresolved uncertainty instead of inventing completion. Require evidence for entity/number changes and retain the original transcript for audit.

Evaluate against human transcripts with a metric that separates beneficial corrections from harmful edits, especially on rare names and silence. An LLM judge alone may reward fluency over fidelity. A lower text-only language-model loss is not proof that the corrected words were spoken.
